source.title: Neuralyzing the Trace: Selective Representation-Level Unlearning with Contrastive Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Itai Zehavi; Fanny Jourdan; Ulrich Aivodji

page_placements.theme: Sparsity, width and extraction choices determine feature granularity

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether sparse-autoencoder features can be extracted and used selectively in LLMs, a new setting for the toy-model superposition claim. It does not reproduce the toy-network setup.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports a PCA energy comparison (3,787,695 for background top-three energy versus 11,517 for background-orthogonal forget residuals, about 329×), but this is evidence about energy bias in extraction, not a measurement of superposition geometry, so it is not a row for these versions. Hyperparameter-search outcomes are not recorded as rows because they are used for model selection. The main benchmark plots report intervention outcomes; rows below capture the text-described SCALPEL-versus-standard-SAE trade-off and the feature-selectivity diagnostics.
record.test_reason: This is an unlearning-method paper. It uses sparse autoencoders as a tool and reports how well its own contrastive SAE (SCALPEL) performs against a standard SAE, NMF, RMU and Gradient Difference on target selectivity and the TOFU forget–utility trade-off. It does not test whether LLMs store features in superposition, whether features are spread across neurons, or whether SAEs recover the model's features in general. It also does not examine polysemanticity, toy models or feature dimensionality. Its diagnostics compare extractors built for author-level unlearning, so they measure method performance rather than any version of the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that reconstruction-based extractors lack selectivity for narrow, low-energy targets. They report that contrastive SCALPEL features improve over NMF and standard SAE interventions and are competitive with RMU and Gradient Difference across Qwen, Llama and Gemma on TOFU. They stress this is an inference-time filter, not certified deletion.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains contrastive sparse autoencoders on residual-stream activations from finetuned LLMs and subtracts selected decoded features for unlearning. It does not run a toy-network superposition experiment; details of the original source's method are not stated in this text.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper varies extractor method and intervention strength. It states that the extraction layer is fixed at −4 and that systematic layer selection is left for future work.

fits_no_version.finding: On Qwen layer −4, reconstruction-only SAE codes show no target–background separation for author-level targets (ΔC ≈ −0.01; mean top-5 selectivity ≈ 1.9). Background PCA energy is about 329× that of background-orthogonal forget residuals.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reconstruction-trained SAEs underrepresent narrow, low-energy concepts and blend them into high-energy background features (energy bias of dictionary learning).

record.problems: The feature-geometry diagnostics are limited to Qwen. The evaluation uses TOFU and three relatively small models. Geometry and feature-selectivity diagnostics do not report uncertainty in the text. The authors note that the perturbation bound concerns expected representation-space magnitude, not downstream behavior or worst-case effects, and that feature scores ignore decoder-direction orientation.
record.rows_left_out: No diagnostic rows for Llama or Gemma were reported: the text says their benchmark behavior is similar, but feature-geometry and top-feature-selectivity diagnostics are reported for Qwen. Other metrics in the main benchmark are not separately transcribed because the text does not give their numeric values.

untested.parts: All of it: toy networks, overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transition.
All of it: neuron polysemanticity and capacity competition.
All of it: non-capacity origins of polysemanticity.
Whether LLM features are spread across neurons, and whether an SAE recovers sparse features in general. The paper only compares extractors for narrow unlearning targets.
Completeness, stability and canonicity of SAE features.

record.verdict_notes: The reader classified this as T3 testing V4. It is better seen as T4: the SAE is the study's tool, and all rows are comparisons of the study's method against baselines. The standard-SAE selectivity failure is a construct related to dictionary-feature coverage (closest to V5's completeness), but it concerns narrow targets and unlearning selectivity, so it is recorded under fits_no_version rather than given a verdict.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks with more sparse features than dimensions, their overlap geometry, and sparsity-dependent transitions.
Neuron polysemanticity and competition for neuron capacity.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise through mechanisms other than capacity pressure.

The study tests extraction and use of target-selective sparse features in author-level TOFU unlearning, not general feature coverage across LLM activations, features spread across neurons, or broad feature dictionaries. The feature-geometry diagnostics are reported for Qwen; Llama and Gemma are included in the unlearning benchmark.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units of model representation.
Whether the underlying model features are inherently one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

relation.reason: SAE feature extraction supplies the intervention mechanism; the reported comparisons concern narrow-target selectivity and forgetting–utility trade-offs.

tranche.reason: Uses sparse dictionaries for targeted unlearning and evaluates extraction selectivity and intervention performance; these measurements do not directly test the listed superposition versions.

source_check.notes: The 329× ratio compares top-three PCA energies, not total background and forget-manifold energies. The authors-conclusion paraphrase is accurate; the method filters activations at inference and does not establish certified deletion.
